hints: Notice the two different results after unloading: returns to original length first, then stays longer than originally.
Recall that elastic deformation is fully recovered on unloading while plastic deformation leaves a permanent extension.
Compare each stage in turn to those definitions to decide if one stage or both stages match.
walkthrough: Identify the evidence: with lighter weights the spring returns to its original length after the weights are removed.

State the rule: elastic deformation is removed when the load is removed, so the object returns to original length; plastic deformation remains after the load is removed, so a permanent extension is left.
Apply to the first loading: full recovery means the limit of proportionality was not exceeded and elastic deformation is shown.
Apply to the second loading with heavier weights: the spring is longer than originally after unloading, so a permanent set remains and plastic deformation is shown.
Combine both observations: the experiment demonstrates elastic behaviour first and then plastic behaviour. This is option A

options.A: First stage shows elastic return to original length and second stage shows plastic permanent extension, so both types are shown.
options.B: Elastic alone cannot explain the second stage where the spring is longer than originally after unloading.
options.C: Deformation clearly occurred because length changed under load, with return in the first case and permanent change in the second.
options.D: Plastic alone cannot explain the first stage where the spring returned fully to its original length.
